items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I saw two Maharajahs that I had seen in Paris... the other was the Maharaja of Kapurthala

ctx.x: Christmas came and it was the first time I spent a Christmas Eve that I didn't have to wear an overcoat. The whitest thing about that Christmas Eve was the white suit I wore when I went out in the afternoon. We went out often between mid-day and 4 p.m. which was the hour that most people took their siesta. The Indians had a saying that no one went out during those hours except Englishmen and damn fools. Too bad we were not Englishmen.

The Taj was jumping Christmas Eve and Christmas night also, but the biggest ball was New Year's Eve, 1936. The room was filled with English dignitaries, diplomats and Maharajahs. Some brought their families. I saw two Maharajahs that I had seen in Paris, "Chez Florence". One was the Maharaja of Cochin, the other was the Maharaja of Kapurthala who took his European gals with him where ever he went. There were about 6 or 8 of them.

There were some young prince that came and stood near the band stand to dig our jazz like the jazz lovers did at the Savoy. Later in the night when it came time to push the old year out and welcome in the new one, they started throwing cotton balls at us and we threw them back at them. Everybody let their hair down and started having a ball.
